content.title: About
content.content: Taco is a popular Mexican dish consisting of a soft or crunchy corn (sometimes wheat) shell filled with meat, vegetables, cheese, and sauces. The NFS (New Flavor Series) version offers a unique blend of spices and aromas designed for a bolder taste experience.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic taco originated in Mexico in the early 19th century as street food.
The word “taco” comes from Mexican Spanish, meaning “wrapper” or “plug”.
In the United States more than 3 billion tacos are consumed each year, making it one of the most popular fast‑food items.
The NFS variant uses a mix of smoked chipotle, lime zest, and aromatic herbs not found in traditional recipes.
Traditional Mexican tacos are often served with salsa, guacamole, and lime wedges.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Fillings such as beef, chicken, or beans provide quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain shells contain thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain corn shells add dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: When prepared by grilling or baking rather than deep‑frying, tacos contain minimal trans fats, which is better for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Chipotle, paprika, and lime are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sauces and ready‑made seasoning mixes can be salty, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Fatty fillings
items.content: Fatty cuts of meat or large amounts of cheese increase calories and saturated fat levels.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to corn shells.

items.title: Spicy foods
items.content: Hot sauces can irritate the stomach and esophagus in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tacos can be enjoyed warm or hot, filling the shell with meat, beans, fresh vegetables, cheese, and your favorite sauces. For a lighter option, choose whole‑grain shells and lean chicken or turkey fillings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry corn shells in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 2 weeks. Cooked fillings should be kept in the refrigerator and consumed within 3 days.
